subject.title: Feature: Global session reset on auth switch

question: Should global auth refresh cover all persisted sessions across every agent store or only active sessions, and should in-flight runs finish, cancel, or be rejected during credential cutover?
rationale: Current code establishes operator-admin authority for session reset but does not define the cross-agent target set or whether work already using the prior credential identity may continue safely.

options.title: All stores, future turns
options.body: Refresh persisted auth bindings across agent stores while allowing already-started runs to finish with their captured credential identity.

options.title: Active sessions, cancel runs
options.body: Refresh only active sessions and cancel their in-flight runs before accepting new work with current credentials.

options.title: Keep lazy invalidation
options.body: Do not add a bulk operation; retain per-session next-use auth-epoch checks and improve provider-switch tooling and status feedback.

recommendation.title: All stores, future turns
recommendation.body: Refresh persisted auth bindings across agent stores while allowing already-started runs to finish with their captured credential identity.

likelyOwner.reason: The reset service extraction and densest current history across Gateway reset, protocol, and auth-epoch surfaces route this boundary decision here.
